extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners/readers of MPEP)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for preparing, signing, mailing, and prioritizing Office actions and for petitions to make an application special under 37 CFR 1.102. Covers examiner duties (mentioning claims, drafting for pro se applicants), handling returned actions, order-of-examination priorities, and the grounds/requirements for petitions to make special (manufacture, infringement, health, age, environment, energy, prioritized examination).

rubrics_metrics.name: When to limit action on a claim to a particular issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Some situations exist where examination of an application appears best accomplished by limiting action on the claim thereof to a particular issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations include: (A) application too informal for complete action on the merits (MPEP § 702.01); (B) undue multiplicity of claims with no successful telephone election (MPEP § 2173.05(n)); (C) misjoinder of inventions with no successful telephone election (MPEP § 803, § 810, § 812.01); (D) disclosure directed to perpetual motion (Ex parte Payne). For perpetual motion cases, cite best prior art and point out pertinency without specifically applying it to the claims. Conversely, rejections based on res judicata, no prima facie showing for reissue, new matter, or inoperativeness (not involving perpetual motion) should be accompanied by rejection on all other available grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify of inaccuracies in amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should notify applicants of inaccuracies in amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 714, subsection II.G for more detailed guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each claim must be mentioned in every Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: In every Office action, each pending claim should be mentioned by number, and its treatment or status given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a summary of the status of all claims presented for examination. Use Form PTO-326 'Office Action Summary'. Claims retained under 37 CFR 1.142 and 1.146 should be treated as set out in MPEP § 821 to § 821.04(b). Keep the Index of Claims up to date per MPEP § 719.04. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: State when claims are allowable (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: When patentable subject matter is disclosed and apparent from claims/arguments, examiners should indicate when claims are allowable or suggest allowable claim language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pro se applicants, draft one or more claims and indicate they would be allowed if incorporated. Examiner actions should be constructive — offer definite suggestions for correction for form defects or omitted limitations and consider suggesting an interview to reach agreement on allowable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may draft claims for pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining a pro se (inventor-filed) application and patentable subject matter is apparent, examiner should draft claims for the applicant and indicate such claims would be allowed if incorporated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expedites prosecution and is expected in cases where applicant appears unfamiliar with proper preparation and prosecution. If suggested claims are not embraced by the original oath/declaration, require supplemental oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.67. Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.43, 7.97) when indicating allowable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable except as to form — constructive suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: If application discloses patentable subject matter but claims cannot be allowed due to formal defects or omitted limitation, do not stop at a bare objection or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer definite suggestions for correction; indicate aspects/features not claimed that could be claimed for favorable consideration; suggest interviews when useful. If a claim is otherwise allowable but depends on a canceled or rejected claim, state it would be allowable if rewritten in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early allowance of clearly allowable claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner is satisfied that the prior art has been fully developed and some claims are clearly allowable, allowance should not be delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.43, 7.43.01, 7.43.02 may be used to indicate allowable subject matter; form paragraph 7.97 may be used to indicate allowance of claims ('Claim [1] allowed').

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use for specific 35 U.S.C. 112 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use specific form paragraphs when dependent or independent claims are rejected solely under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, and would be allowable if amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 7.43.01 for independent/ dependent claims rejected under 112 second paragraph; ¶ 7.43.02 for dependent claims that would be allowable if rewritten to include base claim limitations. Examiner notes specify when to use each paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number paragraphs consecutively in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is good practice to number the paragraphs of the Office action consecutively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive numbering facilitates identification of paragraphs in future prosecution of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questioning results and examples — standard for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of tests and examples should not normally be questioned unless there is a reasonable basis; if questioned, reject appropriate claims as based on insufficient disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must reply by providing actual test/example results or relevant arguments supporting predicted results. Care must be taken that no new matter is entered into the application. See MPEP § 2161–§ 2164.08(c) for written description and enablement discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider 35 U.S.C. 101 when operability/utility questions exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If questions are present as to operability or utility, consider the applicability of a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.03(a) and § 2107 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing and initialing by the examiner who prepared the action
rubrics_metrics.description: After typing, the examiner who prepared the Office action reviews it for correctness and the surname or initials and date typed should appear below the action; if not authorized to sign, initial and forward to authorized signatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact information via form paragraphs 7.100, 7.101 or 7.102. These paragraphs provide exact insertion instructions for name, phone number, workdays, duty hours, supervisor contact, and handling for different schedules (non 5/4/9 and 5/4/9 schedules). For IFW, follow IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing by primary or other authorized examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Although only the original is signed, the word 'Examiner' and the name of the signer should appear on the original and copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All Office actions and correspondence should be signed promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of the original into the file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: The original Office action signed by the authorized examiner is placed in the file wrapper; its character, paper number, and mailing date are entered in black ink on the outside of the file wrapper under 'Contents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stamp mailing date after signing
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date should not be typed when the Office action is written, but should be stamped or printed on all copies after it has been signed and is about to be mailed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing copies and IFW procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the examiner's action are mailed by the Technology Center after the original has been initialed by the assistant examiner and signed by the authorized signatory examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After copies are mailed the original is returned for placement in the file. For IFW processing, see IFW Manual section 3.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling returned Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is returned undelivered by the USPS, Technology Center technical support staff should check the application file to ensure correct correspondence address; if incorrect, remail and stamp 'remailed' with date; the reply period runs from remailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mailed to the correct address but addressed to an attorney or agent, a letter (with copy of the Office action) may be sent to the first named inventor or assignee informing them of the returned action; if remailing elapses with no communication, the application is abandoned. For IFW, add copies of the letter and envelope to IFW as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of examination — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprovisional applications accepted as complete are assigned for examination and shall be taken up in the order in which they have been filed, except for those advanced pursuant to 37 CFR 1.102 or other specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.496 and MPEP § 1893.03 for order of examination of international national stage applications. Each examiner gives priority in docket to the oldest effective U.S. filing date, with limited exceptions authorized by Technology Center Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority categories and giving precedence to certain types of cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of examination gives priority to reissue applications, reexamination proceedings, and other special cases; certain examiner procedures take precedence even over special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top priority to reissue applications in which litigation has been stayed, ex parte reexamination proceedings involved in litigation, and inter partes reexamination proceedings involved in litigation. Priority also to special cases with fixed 30-day due dates (examiner's answers, decisions on motions) and other categories like interferences, petitions, and cases ready for final conclusion. If an examiner is satisfied an application is in condition for allowance or will be finally rejected, act forthwith.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of special cases advanced out of turn
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated list of special cases that may be advanced out of turn for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases include: (A) inventions of peculiar importance to public service on request of head of government department; (B) applications made special by petition; (C) reissues, especially in stayed litigation; (D) applications remanded by appellate tribunal; (E) applications transferred after being taken up; (F) applications appearing to interfere with other allowable applications or unexpired patents; (G) applications ready for allowance or except as to formal matters; (H) applications in condition for final rejection; (I) applications pending more than 5 years (effective pendency >5 years); (J) reexamination proceedings (MPEP § 2261 and § 2661). See MPEP § 714.13, § 1207 and § 1309.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.102 — grounds and procedures to advance examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications will not be advanced out of turn except as provided by regulation, Director order, or upon filing of requests/petitions meeting requirements of paragraphs (b)-(e) of 37 CFR 1.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs include: (b) requests based on public service importance; (c) petitions based on applicant's age or health or environmental/energy/terrorism contributions; (d) petitions on other grounds requiring fee; (e) requests for prioritized examination subject to requirements and fees. Prioritized examination has statutory restrictions (see other rubric entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized examination (1.102(e)) — limits and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination must comply with paragraph (e) requirements and be accompanied by prioritized examination fee, processing fee, and publication fee (if not already paid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for which prioritized examination has been requested may not contain or be amended to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or any multiple dependent claim. Prioritized examination will not be accorded to certain application types (international apps not in national stage, design, reissue, provisional, reexamination). For utility nonprovisional applications, the request must be filed via electronic filing and present upon filing; if filed with or after an RCE, request must be before mailing of first Office action after the RCE. Only one such request may be granted per application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special — good faith and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement in support of a petition to make special must be based on a good faith belief that the invention qualifies for special status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.56 and 10.18 for duty of candor. Petitions filed on/after specific dates must comply with revised program requirements (e.g., August 25, 2006 for revised accelerated program; see MPEP § 708.02(a); September 26, 2011 for prioritized examination under 1.102(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for manufacture — required allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make special on manufacture ground requires fee and a statement by applicant/assignee/registered attorney alleging possession of sufficient available capital and facilities to manufacture or that such will be made available if patent granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include approximate amount of capital and nature of facilities; if prospective manufacturer is an individual, include corroborating statement (e.g., bank officer) showing ability to manufacture. Also state that prospective manufacturer will not manufacture or increase manufacture unless patent will be granted; obligate to manufacture in U.S. upon allowance; state applicant/assignee has made careful prior art search or has good knowledge of pertinent prior art. Provide one copy of each closely related reference if not already of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for actual infringement — required allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to make special due to actual infringement (not prospective) requires fee and a statement alleging actual infringing device/product on market or method in use and a rigid comparison showing claims unquestionably infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must state that a careful prior art search was made or applicant has good knowledge of pertinent prior art. Provide one copy of each closely related reference if not already of record. Do not submit models or specimens of the infringing product unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special based on applicant's health
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special on petition accompanied by evidence showing applicant's health is such that they might not be available to assist in prosecution (doctor's certificate or medical certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee required for such a petition (37 CFR 1.102(c)). Personal/medical information submitted as evidence will be available to the public if the application is public; if applicant does not wish this, submit information pursuant to MPEP § 724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special based on applicant's age
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be made special upon filing a petition including evidence that applicant is 65 years of age or more (applicant statement or practitioner's statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No fee required. Personal information becomes public unless submitted per MPEP § 724.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for environmental quality
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord special status to patent applications for inventions which materially enhance the quality of the environment by contributing to restoration or maintenance of air, water, or soil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must state special status is sought because invention materially enhances environmental quality; no fee required. If disclosure is not clear on its face, petition must be accompanied by a statement explaining how the materiality standard is met. Materiality standard does not permit speculation about hypothetical end-user applications nor permit benefiting from a minor aspect that may enhance the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to make special for energy contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accord special status to inventions which materially contribute to discovery/development of energy resources or to more efficient utilization/conservation of energy resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of category (A) include developments in fossil fuels, hydrogen, nuclear, solar; category (B) includes inventions reducing energy consumption. Petition under 37 CFR 1.102 must state which category is applicable; no fee required. If disclosure is not clear, petition must be accompanied by a statement explaining how the materiality standard is met. Materiality standard precludes speculation or relying on minor aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide references when required for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants making petitions to make special (manufacture, infringement, etc.) must provide one copy of each reference deemed most closely related to the subject matter encompassed by the claims if such references are not already of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps examiners evaluate the petition; failure to provide may impede granting the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit models/specimens of infringing product unless requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Models or specimens of the infringing product or that of the application should not be submitted unless requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certain internal examiner procedures have precedence even over special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Some examiner procedures take precedence over actions on special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: all papers typed and ready for signature should be completed and mailed; issue cases returned with 'Printer Waiting' slip must be processed and returned within indicated period; reissue applications involved in stayed litigation should be given priority.
